decisions.statement: A key the page states already is refused rather than stated anew.
A key is judged before the body is read.
A key spelled as a slug is refused rather than gained under that spelling.
The refusal names the key that spelling makes.
A key that is no bare word is refused rather than gained.
The value is written as one value rather than as a list of one.
The key is written after the property `after` names.
An `after` naming no property the page states is refused rather than dropped.
The key is written last where no `after` is stated.
A body exporting no object is refused rather than gaining a key.
The body is answered rather than written.
The passage answered is the lines the key is put into rather than the body.
A value is put in as the body spells it rather than as a quoted string.
Text that parses as no value is refused before the body is read.
A value is text or a number or a boolean or null or a list or a record of those.
A bare word is refused rather than written in.
The whitespace around a value is dropped before that value is read or written.

definition: one key put into a page's body under one value rather than under a list
